solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Person wedded to the past is around, unfortunately

indicators.note: things gone unfortunately have gone wrong, so the letters of the words before it end up out of order

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in the past is, sadly, still hanging about.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a fossil-like person clinging to outdated ways is called by the name of the extinct reptile.

clue.text: Golf score ascribed to young fellow, a clergyman

parts.note: par is the standard score for a hole in golf
a son is a young male, a boy

explanation.surface: A vicar is credited with a par round, or is the son of one.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish priest in the Church of England is commonly called by this title.

clue.text: Sunny type to settle on one sort of gloomy weather?

parts.note: to opt for something is to choose it, to settle on it
the Roman numeral for one is I
mist is murky, dismal weather

explanation.surface: A cheerful person choosing a dreary day seems contradictory.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunny type has a bright, hopeful outlook, the mark of someone who expects the best.

clue.text: Apartment with little excitement

definitions.meaning: a set of rooms on one floor, the British word for a dwelling of that kind
dull, lacking life or sparkle, as a party or a performance can be

explanation.surface: A rather dull home.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a single-storey dwelling and something lifeless or uninspired.

clue.text: Chess move took effect after most of match

indicators.note: the piece for 'took effect' is placed after the trimmed match
most of a word means it loses its final letter here

parts.note: a match is a game
brakes that bit took effect, gripped

explanation.surface: A chess opening finally worked once the game was well under way.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening in chess that sacrifices material for advantage is known by this term.

clue.text: Good area offering shelter leads to joy

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, out of the wind

explanation.surface: A refuge brings happiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Glee is a synonym of delight, great happiness.

clue.text: Opera-singer keen to make comeback

indicators.note: making a comeback means coming back the way it went, so the word for keen runs backwards

parts.note: avid means keen, eager

explanation.surface: A soprano is eager to return to the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrated female opera star is called a prima donna, or this Italian word for goddess.

clue.text: Obvious two friends will have adopted British English

indicators.note: adopting takes something in, so the British letter goes inside the pair of friends
two signals the word for friend appears twice in a row

parts.note: a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: Clearly, a pair of mates will have taken in a Brit and an Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: The B goes into the second PAL only, giving PAL + PABL, then E finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Palpable means so plain it could almost be touched, hence obvious.

clue.text: A pretentious person backed one sort of miniature gardening

indicators.note: backed here means turned back to front, so the words before it run backwards

parts.note: a snob looks down on others with pretensions of superiority
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A snooty type supported a particular style of tiny gardening.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese art of growing dwarfed trees in pots is a kind of small-scale gardening.

clue.text: Small computer ready for work in motorcycle racing

indicators.note: in places the word for ready for work within the racing letters

parts.note: the TT (Tourist Trophy) is the famous motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
able means capable, fit for the job

explanation.surface: A portable computer is fit for use in bike racing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tablet is a flat, handheld touchscreen device, a compact computer.

clue.text: French bread is a nuisance

explanation.surface: Baguettes can be irritating.
explanation.definitionFit: The French term for a loaf of bread doubles as English slang for an irritating person or thing.

clue.text: A rum time, fooling around like a child

indicators.note: fooling around suggests messing about, so the letters before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: Larking about at an odd hour is childish behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Childish, not yet grown up in behaviour or development.

clue.text: One engaged in skill in theatrical performance beside the sea

indicators.note: in puts the skill-with-one inside the theatrical performance

parts.note: a mime is a wordless theatrical performance

indicators.note: engaged in means occupied within, so the one goes inside the skill

parts.note: art means skill, craft
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: An actor caught up in his craft in a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One engaged in skill' reads like a description of a person, but it is a nested insertion: the numeral goes into the skill first, and that whole piece is then placed in the performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Coastal or nautical, relating to or bordering the sea.

clue.text: Our nave's rebuilt, consuming a great deal

indicators.note: a rebuilt structure is put together anew, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Restoring the church's central aisle is costing a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravenous means voracious, devouring huge amounts out of hunger.

clue.text: Tore round in pursuit of concert impresario

indicators.note: in pursuit of means following, so the jumbled letters come after the concert

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as in the BBC Proms

indicators.note: round suggests going around, so the letters of the word before it are turned about

explanation.surface: Someone dashed about chasing after a show organiser.
explanation.definitionFit: A promoter organises and finances events such as concerts, the role of an impresario.

clue.text: Legendary swimmer, in former manner

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit within the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: A mythical sea creature in old-fashioned style.
explanation.definitionFit: The male counterpart of a mermaid, a creature of folklore living in the sea.

clue.text: Long to take in very shady joint

indicators.note: taking in means holding within, so the very letter goes inside

parts.note: to long for something is to be dying for it, to die

explanation.surface: Desperate to visit a disreputable bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A dive is slang for a seedy, disreputable bar or club.

clue.text: Bravery has beloved losing heart

indicators.note: losing heart means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: darling means a beloved person

explanation.surface: Courage is shown by a sweetheart who is dispirited.
explanation.definitionFit: Daring as a noun means boldness, courage in taking risks.

clue.text: Glamorous person at head of church shows formality

indicators.note: at head of puts the star in front of the church

parts.note: a star is a celebrity, a glamorous figure

explanation.surface: A celebrity leading a congregation displays stiffness.
explanation.definitionFit: Starch figuratively means stiff, prim formality of manner.

clue.text: Up-to-the-minute news excluding the French sporting event

indicators.note: excluding means leaving out, so the French article is removed

parts.note: the latest is the most recent news
la is a French word for the

explanation.surface: Breaking news without French coverage of a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A Test is an international cricket (or rugby) match, a major fixture.

clue.text: Bad weather is welcome!

definitions.meaning: frozen pellets of ice falling from the sky
a greeting, a call of salute

explanation.surface: A storm greets visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: Icy precipitation shares its spelling with an old exclamation of greeting or acclaim.

clue.text: Crowd mostly drawn to European ruler's position

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is used

parts.note: a throng is a crowd

explanation.surface: A crowd is largely attracted to a continental monarch's seat.
explanation.definitionFit: The ceremonial seat of a monarch, and by extension sovereign power.

clue.text: Representation of space is start of much fantasy

indicators.note: a representation presents something in a new form, so these letters are reworked
start of takes the first letter of the word after it

explanation.surface: Depicting outer space is the beginning of much science fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Retreating into fantasy to avoid real life is known as this.

clue.text: Pointless seeing reduction in common sense

indicators.note: reduction means being cut short, so the phrase loses its last letter

parts.note: pointless means of no use

explanation.surface: It is futile to cut back on good sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Nous is British informal for practical intelligence, gumption.
